Curiosity’s Radiation Assessment Detector · Sol 1 · 7 August 2012 UTC

Historical instrument data

These are absorbed dose rates in the rover’s detectors. Crew exposure requires onboard dosimetry. The archive stays separate from crew readings and health status.

Source and method

NASA Planetary Data System dataset MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0. The chart uses all 14 observations from RAD_RDR_2012_220_02_25_0001_V00. The dose-rate values come directly from the archive. The extraction converts ordinal dates to UTC calendar timestamps and checks each value against the label’s byte offsets.

Crew guide

Measurement instructions and what to do when readings change.

Taking measurements

Five spaceflight hazards

Space radiation
Use onboard dosimetry and mission event records to review exposure. Explore NASA’s Mars radiation measurements.
Isolation and confinement
Sleep and mood records can help crew members notice and discuss changes.
Distance from Earth
Follow the onboard protocol when communications are delayed. Download a report for the next contact window.
Altered gravity
Compare heart rate and blood pressure at similar activity levels and postures. Follow the mission plan for separate bone health measurements.
Hostile or closed environments
Review changes in sleep or well-being alongside cabin conditions. Tell the crew if several people report similar changes.
NASA Human Research Program ↗

Reading the status labels

Training uses synthetic crew readings. The personal log compares recent measurements with your own history. If a reading changes, check the conditions, log the context and follow the mission medical protocol. Report serious symptoms to the onboard medic immediately.
